marks.gloss_en: והדר פשטו לה מברייתא: since the baraita gives צאת הכוכבים as the siman, 'uva hashemesh' must be the sun's setting and vetaher the clearing of the day
'uva hashemesh' is the sun's setting (not the light's departure), and vetaher means the day clears -- the priests eat teruma from nightfall
ואנחנו עושים במלאכה... מעלות השחר עד צאת הכוכבים -- the workday runs dawn to starrise, so night begins at צאת הכוכבים (זכר לדבר)
the operative marker for nightfall (when the priests may eat teruma) is the emergence of the stars
וכי תימא: מכי ערבא שמשא ליליא הוא, ואינהו דמחשכי ומקדמי -- perhaps night begins at sunset and they simply worked late and started early, so the verse shows nothing
Rabba bar Rav Shila: had the verse meant the man's purification it would say veyithar; vetaher means the day clears -- so 'uva hashemesh' is sunset
the poor man's mealtime and the priest's teruma-time are one and the same measure
the poor man's mealtime and ordinary people's mealtime are one and the same measure
the poor man's measure and the priest's measure are distinct
R' Meir's marker is twilight as R' Yehuda defines it
R' Meir: I was speaking of R' Yose's twilight, not yours
